page: Vultr vcg-a16-2c-8g-2vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core and 2 threads. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3. System memory consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a fractional 0.125 NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU with 2 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 50 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between general compute and specialized workloads. The instance demonstrates weak multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3465.56 and a PassMark CPU score of 3668.28. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block transfers at 27.11 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 19.81 GB/sec. Database operations are poor, as evidenced by a PassMark database score of 989.35 and a Redis SET throughput of 3.52 million operations per second. However, the GPU-accelerated architecture excels in specific AI tasks, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing for a small 135M model at 7078.28 tokens per second, alongside average performance for text generation on the same model (233.47 tokens per second) and prompt processing on a medium 7B model (117.16 tokens per second).

This instance offers an entry-level entry point into GPU-accelerated computing by partitioning physical GPU resources. This fractional allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require GPU instruction sets but do not demand a full dedicated card. The hardware profile is configured for lightweight LLM inference, small-scale model testing, and basic parallel processing tasks. It is less appropriate for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput web serving, or heavy multi-threaded CPU computations due to the observed bottlenecks in memory bandwidth and multi-core processing.
description: Vultr vcg-a16-2c-8g-2vram is a fractional GPU server configured with 2 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs, 8.0 GB of RAM, and a 50 GB NVMe SSD. It incorporates a 0.125 slice of an NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU, providing 2 GB of VRAM. Performance benchmarks indicate weak multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth capabilities, with a PassMark CPU score of 3668.28 and large-block memory read speeds of 27.11 GB/sec. However, the instance delivers top-tier performance in small-model LLM prompt processing, reaching 7078.28 tokens per second. This server represents a budget-friendly option for developers requiring GPU acceleration without the cost of a full dedicated GPU. It is appropriate for lightweight machine learning inference, model prototyping, and low-intensity parallel processing workloads, while being poorly configured for database operations or heavy multi-threaded CPU tasks.
